item.content:encoded:
Sorry for the thread resurrection here, but I'd like to +1 the "F-14s didn't carry bombs at that time" thing. Simply put, you're incorrect, and I have bona fides about my expertise if needed. The F-14 at the time was a fleet defense interceptor, with no air-to-ground use.

My day job involves the jet in my profile pic, and the F-15A/B/C/D is an air superiority fighter that has never carried a bomb. The F-15E, which is my jet and is actually substantially different from the A/B/C/D, carries many bombs.

The F-14 didn't carry air-to-ground munitions, and certainly not a Paveway I due to lack of a laser designator on-board. While an offboard laser designation is a possibility, you'd need another aircraft such as an A-6 or F-4 to do it. Unless the Foundation sponsored an expensive naval weapons certification program and tactics development in complete secret, and mounted targeting pods, there's no way a F-14 drops a bomb in '71.

More on the F-14 and targeting pods: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LANTIRN#LANTIRN_and_the_F-14_Tomcat

And a quick note about weaponeering - Paveway I/IIs tend to sag due to their bang-bang guidance, and Paveway IIIs with completely different guidance logic don't come out for another decade. It's actually decently difficult to get the bomb to fuse correctly on the right point of the target given those limitations and inconsistent laser reflection off of water. A Walleye 1000lb bomb would be the most likely weapon for use on the targets given the Navy preference for them.

item.content:encoded:
While it might not be intentionally connected to 610 or Sarkicism, it falls into the same issue that so many of those other SPCs also have: The "horror" is over-the-top B-movie/FPS video game plot kind of stuff, liberally strewn with the author's off-the-cuff "what are the worst things ever ever?" subjects — wherein those "worst things" inevitably end up being the exact same luridities that get bludgeoned around in equally cheap fiction. Cannibalism, check, rape, check, body horror, check, season with a generous dollop of religious-themed craziness, serve with the most blatantly unsubtle redactions this side of 231.

My vote's a neutral one. This isn't an invalid way to write horror, and the Sarkic-flavored business (intentionally invoked or not) remains fun to read, but it's ultimately pretty shallow.

I'll also readily admit that reading a comment beforehand that suggested the entity behind 093 might actually have been pulling the strings here tilts things slightly more in my favor.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's telling on how desensitized I am to these kinds of things when I look at this and just go "Oh, it's just a Sarkic Skip". Body Horror, check. Crazy religious-ness, check. Threat to the world as we know it, check. It didn't really terrify me as much as it did others, if only because I kept thinking of how much it reminded me of some other things I'd seen before (The Tleilaxu Tanks, for example, and the religious ranting brought to mind some Prophet Comstock—which is a really interesting comparison to make, now that I think about it)

Now, don't take that as a bad thing; I thought this was a pretty good Skip and worthy of an Upvote (which I have given), but. My only real issue, and this is ine that other people have noted, is that it doesn't really feel like a Skip. I mean, the Foundation only had a minimal (albeit crucial) presence in dealing with 'The Colony'; so minimal that they don't even have Containment Procedures for this and assume that it's gone. So, all we babe is a story.

And it's a good story, don't get me wrong (the UIU, actually relevant and useful for once!? Woo-Hoo!), but that's the thing. It feels more like a story or a Tale then it does a Skip. It's good, but it just feels like it's the wrong spot—a spot it would better serve as a Tale or its own unique Canon.

Still, at the end of the day, I did admit you were able to make something that genuinely made me feel at least Disturbed (even if I felt like I'd seen it before). And, even if I may criticise it's spot and such, that's commendable.

+1
(Apologies in advance if this came off as rude or needlessly critical, that was not my intent)

item.title: Photos
item.content:encoded:
Kaktus, it'd be really helpful if you could supply provenance for those photos. Thanks.

edit: okay, let's see what I can find by myself first. Photo #1, man with microscope, is actor E. G. Marshall (as Doctor David Craig from the television program The Bold Ones: The New Doctors). Photo is public domain as per Wikimedia Commons.

Photo #2, the adults with the little girl, is taken from http://www.oldladywood.co.uk/memories3.htm; Valerie Mears says "These photo's were taken on holiday with my parents and sister Rita", so I assume the people are Valerie-or-Rita and her parents. Photo is not public domain.

Photo #3, the dockworkers, is from the Harry Bridges Center for Labor Studies at the University of Washington; I haven't found the original image yet (because their website isn't as well organized as it could be) but I'm pretty sure photo is not public domain.

Photo #4, the "instance of SCP-2610-E", is a deformed goat (apparently from overexposure to pesticides) born in Argentina. Finding the original photo is difficult, but I've seen some that are watermarked "(C) CEN". It was in 2014, so the copyright's still active.

Photo #5, the warehouse, is "Abandoned gothic Lehigh Valley railroad warehouse ruins in Black Tom. It survived the massive sabotage munitions explosion of 1916. By the early 1960s, it was a relic of another time. Jersey City, New Jersey. 1960". Source: https://www.flickr.com/photos/wavz13/6773196975 — note that this is 'all rights reserved'.

Photo #6, the train wreck, is the May 13 2015 Amtrak wreck outside Philadelphia. Photo is copyright NBC News.

Photo #7, the pregnant woman, is "a pregnant woman and her friend wait as a motorcycle is unhitched from a car, as they prepare to leave Max Yasgur's Bethil farm and the Woodstock music festival". Photo is copyright "Three Lions", licensed via Getty Images. http://www.gettyimages.com/license/3421634
